requirements.observable: The authenticated principal and assurance context, never a caller-supplied actor field, identify every request.
requirements.verification: OIDC user and workload-token positive cases; forged actor, wrong issuer, audience and expired token are rejected without a request record promoted to protected state.

requirements.observable: A versioned mandate binds subject, delegation chain, actions, resources, constraints and expiry; incompatible changes make approvals stale.
requirements.verification: Public API/CLI readback plus subject, version, delegation, constraint and expiry negative cases; no aggregate score substitutes for a rule decision.

requirements.observable: The exact authorization and parameters are rechecked in the transaction that commits a simulated ledger effect.
requirements.verification: Ledger before/after assertions for allowed action and no mutation for missing, expired, revoked, wrong-subject or out-of-scope mandates.

requirements.observable: Revocation and commitment use a defined serialization point; after accepted revocation no new commit succeeds, while earlier commits remain visible.
requirements.verification: Concurrent revoke/commit test records transaction order, restarts the store and proves the resulting ledger and evidence state.

requirements.observable: Approval binds the canonical action digest and enforces requester/approver separation.
requirements.verification: Changed amount, currency, beneficiary or resource invalidates approval; self-approval and reused approval are denied without ledger mutation.

requirements.observable: Idempotency binds key to canonical content; lost response becomes unknown and is reconciled before any retry.
requirements.verification: Same key/same content returns prior state, same key/different content conflicts, crash-after-commit reconciles exactly one ledger entry after restart.

requirements.observable: Intent, identity, mandate, policy, decision, commit and observed result form a hash-linked, attributable evidence chain retaining denials and unknown states.
requirements.verification: Export verification with separately acquired key and anchor detects altered content, reorder and omission under the anchor and contains no secret.

requirements.observable: Every policy has one persisted versioned source, shared Go/API/CLI validation, non-mutating preview, stale-write rejection and Admin editing.
requirements.verification: Preview leaves revision unchanged; apply/read/reopen use the same effective values; stale revision and invalid units are rejected; zero and inheritance semantics are asserted.

requirements.observable: Strict Biba rules protect official objects; only named trusted admission procedures can endorse lower-integrity input into protected state.
requirements.verification: API, CLI and storage tests deny read-down/write-up/invoke-up paths, forged levels and direct writes; authorized endorsement persists provenance and survives restart.

requirements.observable: Project and Business Process applications remain separately buildable while exposing textual action states and blocking reasons in FR/EN and both themes.
requirements.verification: Browser journeys cover keyboard, Escape/focus restoration, 320/390/mobile widths, loading/empty/error/success and failed requests in etat/sombre and FR/EN.

requirements.observable: Public operations demonstrate actual ledger mutation, denial without mutation, restart persistence and concurrency on one exact candidate.
requirements.verification: Named Python recipes and Go tests record assertions and observed state; controls and independent review bind the same candidate SHA.

requirements.observable: Current FR/EN documentation, reproducible recipe, R01-R20 matrix and final RETEX distinguish local controls, engine receipts, review and acceptance.
requirements.verification: Artifact inventory and candidate hashes are complete; unresolved or untested criteria remain open; RETEX follows complete-system qualification.

requirements.observable: OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE authenticates people and private_key_jwt client credentials authenticate services; security attributes, delegation and revocation are enforced.
requirements.verification: Isolated issuer fixtures cover lifecycle, group/role mapping, key rotation, revocation, step-up and separation of duties; no third-party account is created.

requirements.owner: T4 / data policy and execution boundary
requirements.observable: Classification, destination, provider/tool allowlists and per-action secret grants apply on every actually controlled path; an unproven path fails closed.
requirements.verification: Isolated exfiltration, symlink/path escape, direct binary, network destination and secret-scope attacks are denied with no sensitive output persisted.

requirements.owner: T5 / process definition and case services
requirements.observable: Versioned process definitions drive cases, validations and exceptions with history through public operations and a separately deliverable Business Process UX.
requirements.verification: Definition version pinning, case transition, invalid transition, exception authorization, restart and separate frontend build recipes pass.

requirements.owner: T6 / durable evidence and key service
requirements.observable: Signing-key rotation/revocation, independent anchors, retention and exports preserve attribution and detect alteration or omission below a known anchor.
requirements.verification: Old/new/revoked key cases, independent anchor acquisition, retention boundary and tamper/reorder/omission tests pass without exporting secrets.

requirements.observable: Versioned adversarial scenarios replay in isolated roots with no production effect and persist policy, inputs, outcomes and limitations.
requirements.verification: Escape attempts, fixture contamination and production connector selection fail; deterministic replay produces attributable results after reopen.

requirements.observable: A versioned connector SPI supports simulated billing and a second sensitive simulated connector with service invariants, authorization, isolation, idempotency and reconciliation.
requirements.verification: Contract suite runs against both connectors, rejects capability overstatement and direct bypass, and reconciles unknown results without duplicate effect.

requirements.observable: Target-context applicability maps controls, evidence and gaps without claiming certification or global compliance from local tests.
requirements.verification: Each mapping names scope, rationale, evidence owner, status and missing external assessment; unsupported claims are rejected in review.

requirements.observable: An optional separate eBPF collector attributes project process, file and network observations to mission/task/attempt while reporting permission, loss, cleanup and measured overhead.
requirements.verification: Real-kernel recipe proves owned PIDs/events and overhead with/without collection; foreign PID exclusion, lost-event visibility, cleanup, restart and unavailable-capability cases are explicit.

boundaries.control: strict Biba plus narrow attributed endorsement procedures
authorization recheck and ledger mutation in one serializable transaction
capability manifest, mandatory mediation, content-bound idempotency and reconciliation
candidate/input hashes, preserved originals, anchor digests and freshness guards
work/agent attribution, pagination and retention-gap visibility; not immutable business proof
hash chain, signing key lifecycle, separately acquired anchor, omission/reorder detection

boundaries.control: inventory and deny configuration unless containment is demonstrated; eBPF observation alone is not enforcement

interfaces.rule: caller actor fields are ignored; raw tokens and secrets are never persisted in action evidence

Exact operator-managed resource classification is required; caller metadata cannot downgrade it. Local public/internal paths are local-ledger/swarm/simulated-settlement and local-process-state/swarm/process-workflow, with exact tuple checks. Admission rechecks stored digest-bound context before mutation and replay disclosure. Sensitive providers and external effects remain unqualified.

Implemented only for sealed-attestation/local-attestation: persistent server holds ephemeral material in memory, issues a revision/session/action-bound single-attempt grant, persists metadata without raw material, and transfers through a pipe only after the fixed helper proves containment. Restart loses material and denies old grants; provider connectors and sensitive business effects remain unsupported targets. Clients require positive protected readiness before raw transfer. No raw material in business API replies, evidence or agent copies. With data_policy active, restricted/local-attestation/swarm/sealed-attestation must be explicitly allowlisted at preparation, before raw HTTP read, memory load, grant and consumption. The action resource retains separate admission. Computed optional data_context is bound by swarm-secret-delivery-v1; absent policy preserves the exact legacy attestation input. Running helper image is pinned by descriptor; arbitrary providers remain unsupported.
Published immutable FR/EN graph, I3 publisher, expected prior version; normal graph acyclic and ending, explicit admin exception edges. No executable commands or automatic payment approval.

Latest exact version at creation; fixed thereafter. Current authenticated membership, roles, integrity and data policy before transitions and replay disclosure; revision/digests bind decisions. Shared atomic state and identity-linked evidence; no T2 effect linkage in this slice.

Schema3 domain-separated Ed25519 signature binds canonical export v2; trusted public key and lifecycle metadata acquired separately, never self-selected by export. Retired historical keys remain verifiable within period, revoked pins deny acceptance. Old offline pins do not learn later revocations automatically. Optional caller-supplied trusted_checkpoint carries an independently acquired anchor and pin; verifier rejects rollback or divergent prefix, checking canonical original bytes. Absence is explicit checkpoint_verified:false; operator storage is not physically immutable.

Persist only public key identity/digest/proposer/period/configuration and lifecycle. Different I3 activates exact candidate; I3 emergency revocation is immediate. Private key remains protected runtime-only; restart/configuration/expiry fails closed, new rotation required. This does not deliver retention or outside production attestation.

Copy exact signed prefix and originals without replacing files; content-addressed regular private payload plus attributed registry receipt. Existing evidence_retention_days is a minimum hold captured at copy creation and never shortened by later policy reduction. Explicit current I3 release only after elapsed whole days, with no copy/original deletion. Preview is pure; identical orphan publication recoverable, missing/corrupt/link payload fails even on replay. Local operator-controlled storage is not immutable against the same UID; archived pins do not learn later revocations.

Closed content-addressed versioned corpus, canonical uint64 seed string, known unique scenarios and fixed local-ledger-simulation-v1 connector. Caller paths/commands/URLs/production selectors are rejected. The parent creates an empty owned fixture and launches only its fixed Landlock/seccomp helper; fourteen OS boundary assertions precede Trust scenarios. Fixture policy/time are corpus inputs rather than production configuration.

Reserve each attributed attempt before execution, run outside business lock, then revalidate current authority/revision/policy before positive publication. Preserve inputs/corpus/policy/outcomes; exact request replay creates nothing, explicit replay creates a linked new attempt and compares deterministic digest. Owner loss stays visible and never refunds attempts. Parent cancellation/death stops fixed child; a hard server crash can leave owned fixture files until explicit cleanup. Simulated results are not provider or eBPF evidence.
canonical digest changes on every covered field and invalidates incompatible approvals
canonical parameter schema is connector-owned; unknown fields are rejected
requester and approver separation is enforced from authenticated identities
only an admitted protected intent crosses the connector boundary
states are denied, committed, unknown or reconciled; unknown is never retried before connector readback
payload references exclude secrets; export includes anchor metadata and verification recipe
manifest declares action/resource schema, isolation and capabilities; direct plugin network/filesystem access outside granted boundary is denied
Unix transport authenticates peer credentials; business decisions and payload secrets never originate here

alternatives.description: Reuse launch-time agent authorization and post-hoc validation only.
limits: authority can expire or be revoked before effect
post-hoc evidence cannot prevent an effect

alternatives.description: Add canonical per-action admission, exact approval digest, transactional authorization at effect time and mandatory connector mediation.
advantages: revocation and concurrency have a serialization point
negative paths can assert no business mutation
limits: requires new domain store/API/CLI/Admin and connector containment
cannot claim protection for uninventoried direct paths

alternatives.description: Use eBPF/LSM as the primary authorization or effect blocker.
advantages: kernel-level visibility and possible enforcement on selected hooks
limits: privileged, kernel-dependent and hard to map to business semantics
observation probes do not establish authorization
cannot replace service invariants or transaction-level idempotency
